resources.string: Add origins, insertions, innervation, clinical pearls, or exam reminders…
Tap any organ, bone, vessel, or nerve in the 3D Atlas to bookmark it or write offline study notes.
Try searching by anatomical name, FMA/part ID, or a keyword from your notes.

BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science (DBCLS), licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).

Source geometry: isa_BP3D_4.0_obj_99.zip (BodyParts3D 4.0) with IS-A and PART-OF anatomical hierarchy tables (2,234 meshes and 3,432 named FMA concepts).

Publication: Mitsuhashi et al. (2009), BodyParts3D: 3D structure database for anatomical concepts. Nucleic Acids Research, doi:10.1093/nar/gkn613.

Adaptations: Axes converted from millimeters/Z-up to meters/Y-up, simplified via meshoptimizer (0.2% relative error limit), normals quantized to signed 16-bit, packed into binary chunks with curated system groupings and colors.

Disclaimer: Represents an adult male reference anatomy for educational study only. Not a diagnostic or clinical tool.
